articles.title: How WhatsApp clue, Mygate trail help CBI crack NEET paper leak
articles.description: A WhatsApp conversation triggered the CBI's probe into the NEET-UG examination scam. Subject matter experts colluded by memorizing exam questions and distributing them to students for a fee. Tracking through Mygate app logs and WhatsApp groups led investigators to the involved students and question setters. Additionally, papers were smuggled to Rajasthan, where coaching centers disseminated the leaked materials. The CBI's chargesheet scrutinizes the organized gang's exploitation of NTA's weaknesses.

articles.title: 'Why should entire city suffer?': Delhi HC on plea for protest at Jantar Mantar
articles.description: Concerns were voiced by the Delhi High Court regarding Jantar Mantar as a protest site, questioning why the city should endure interruptions from protests. A Dalit Christian group has sought permission to hold a peaceful demonstration on August 10, while the police have been tasked to provide clarity on the request by Saturday. Additionally, the Supreme Court is considering other potential protest locations.

articles.description: Thomas Aquinas championed the notion of disseminating wisdom for the greater good of society. True expertise is demonstrated through the ability to clarify ideas and enhance collective understanding.

articles.title: Onion, oil or chicken: What made your thali costlier in July
articles.description: In July, the prices for home-cooked thalis surged compared to the previous year, with vegetarian options increasing by four percent and non-vegetarian increasing by nine percent. The rise in costs was driven by expensive onions, vegetable oil, and LPG for vegetarian meals, while non-vegetarian thalis were notably affected by higher broiler chicken prices. Nevertheless, the decline in potato and tomato prices somewhat alleviated these overall increases.

articles.title: India has 86,360 postgraduate medical seats; Centre approves plan to add 5,000 more by 2028-29
articles.description: The Centre has informed Parliament that India now has 86,360 postgraduate medical seats and plans to add 5,000 more by 2028-29 under a revamped infrastructure scheme. The expansion, backed by higher funding and updated regulatory norms, aims to strengthen specialist medical training, improve healthcare capacity and address the country's growing demand for qualified doctors.

articles.title: Effort recession is here: Why Gen Z is no longer glorifying overwork, and what it means for the future of work
articles.description: A new workplace trend called the "effort recession" suggests Gen Z is redefining commitment rather than abandoning it. As AI reshapes productivity and burnout concerns grow, younger employees are prioritising meaningful work, flexibility and wellbeing over long hours. Experts say organisations must earn discretionary effort through trust, purpose and empathetic leadership instead of expecting constant overwork.

articles.title: In 1981, Harvard rejected Paul Devlin; he spotted a grammatical error, rejected the rejection and had his response published in The New York Times
articles.description: In 1981, high school student Paul Devlin responded to Harvard University's rejection letter by rejecting its rejection instead. Inspired by a grammatical error in Harvard's letter, his witty reply was published byThe New York Times. More than four decades later, the letter has resurfaced online and continues to entertain readers.
